index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents the architecture of the GLoG-CSUnet model, divided into four main components labeled (a), (b), (c), and (d). 

[1] Global Layout and Structure: The overall layout is split into two primary sections. On the right, part (a) shows the full segmentation pipeline, which begins with an 'Image' input and proceeds through a series of processing stages before outputting 'segmentation'. On the left, part (b) details the 'Token Embedding' or 'Patch Embedding' module, which is a subcomponent of the main pipeline. Below these, parts (c) and (d) provide close-up views of the 'LoG Transformation Learning Unit' and 'Gabor Transformation Learning Unit', respectively, which are internal components of the embedding module.

[2] Visual Modules and Attributes: In part (a), the segmentation pipeline starts with a dashed red rectangle labeled 'Patch Embedding', which feeds into a series of three identical processing blocks. Each block contains a purple rounded rectangle labeled 'CST Block x2' (Convolutional Swin Transformer Block repeated twice), followed by a pink rounded rectangle labeled 'Patch merging'. These blocks are arranged vertically in a descending order, indicating a hierarchical downsampling process. From each CST block, a blue arrow leads to a small circular node labeled 'sc' (skip connection), which then connects to a corresponding block on the right side of the diagram. The right side consists of three mirrored blocks, each containing a purple 'CST Block x2' and a green 'Up sampling' block, arranged vertically in ascending order. These up-sampling blocks receive skip connections from the left side and are connected sequentially. The topmost up-sampling block feeds into a yellow 'Patch expanding' block, which in turn connects to a final yellow 'Linear Projection' block, leading to the 'segmentation' output. The entire pipeline is enclosed in a light gray background.

Part (b) details the 'Token Embedding' module, enclosed in a large dashed red oval. It contains two parallel learning units: a peach-colored rounded rectangle labeled 'Gabor Transformation Learning Unit x N' and a pale yellow one labeled 'LoG Transformation Learning Unit x M'. Each has a pink sub-box specifying 'Conv k=3x3, out channels=N' and 'Conv k=3x3, out channels=M', respectively. Outputs from both units feed into a blue oval labeled 'Concat', which combines them. The concatenated output is then processed through a sequence of four pink rectangular blocks, each representing a 'Conv k=3x3' layer with varying output channels: C/2, C/2, C, and C, where C = N+M+1. Each convolutional layer is followed by a 'GELU' activation function, except the third, which also includes '+LN' (Layer Normalization). The final output is passed through another 'GELU' before exiting the module.

Parts (c) and (d) show the internal structure of the LoG and Gabor units. Part (c) has a pale yellow background and displays a white box labeled 'Learning Parameter' with 'σ' inside, connected by an arrow to a grid labeled 'LoG Filter' (n×n). Part (d) has a peach background and shows a vertical stack of five white boxes labeled with learning parameters: λ, γ, φ, σ, θ, connected by an arrow to a similar n×n grid labeled 'Gabor Filter'.

[3] Connections and Arrows: In part (a), arrows indicate the flow: from 'Image' to 'Patch Embedding', then down through the three 'CST Block x2' and 'Patch merging' blocks. Skip connections (blue arrows) go from each 'CST Block x2' to a 'sc' node, which then points to the corresponding 'CST Block x2' on the right. The right-side blocks are connected vertically via black arrows, with 'Up sampling' blocks receiving input from the previous block and the 'sc' nodes. The final 'Linear Projection' outputs to 'segmentation'. In part (b), blue arrows connect the Gabor and LoG units to the 'Concat' node, which then feeds into the sequence of convolutional layers. In parts (c) and (d), single black arrows point from the parameter boxes to the respective filters.
